Please direct all further communications regarding this matter to the undersigned.

Very truly yours,

[Outside counsel]
Counsel for Juniper Health Staffing, LLC

# Assessment — Juniper Health Staffing v. Pinecrest Senior Living (Session 1, rev. 2)

**Privileged & confidential — attorney work product.** Prepared for D. Okonkwo, CEO, Juniper Health Staffing, LLC.
Date: October 26, 2026. Rev. 2 incorporates the client's answers of the same date (Bell's confirmation of the waiver; the $3,100 June double-enters; the "unread template" reaction to Exhibit C). All citations are to the reference library (`library/INDEX.md`); anything outside it is labeled **[not in library — unverified]**.

---

## 1. Bottom line (plain words)

The CEO's $862,000 target **is not supportable from our own file**, and a lawsuit is **not available** — the contract requires arbitration. The unanswered Exhibit C does **not** kill us; it redirects us (see § 6).

| Component of CEO demand | Amount | Our assessment |
|---|---:|---|
| Unpaid invoices (5) | $340,000.00 | **$265,200 strong** (4 invoices deemed accepted). J-4533: Juniper's own review found $3,100 of double-enters → adjusted **$71,700**, and the client says the rest is legit — assertable, with audit-fight risk |
| Conversion fees (7 × 25% × $64,000 avg) | $112,000.00 | **$80,000 assertable (5 hires).** Two hires (Rosa, Tay) were waived in writing Feb 11, 2026 — minus $32,000. Bell: "Just those two. I never agreed to the other five." |
| Lost profits / "tortious interference" (12 mo.) | $410,000.00 | **~$0.** Barred by the contract's consequential-damages clause and by Columbia tort law on our facts |
| **CEO total** | **$862,000.00** | |
| Late interest (§2, 1%/mo), accrued to 2026-10-25 | +$8,847.50 | Add (arithmetic § 4) |
| June double-enters credited | −$3,100.00 | Concede proactively (letter ¶2) |
| **Maximum good-faith demand** | **$425,747.50** | Of which **$274,047.50 is the high-confidence core** |

We must **not** demand the Rosa/Tay conversion fees or the $410,000 interference claim: our own documents (the Feb 11 Bell email; §6 of the contract) contradict them, and Rule 3.1 bars asserting claims without a non-frivolous basis while Rule 1.4 requires us to tell the client the adverse facts (Columbia R. Prof'l Conduct 1.4, 3.1; *fee_shifting_and_candor.md*). A demand letter is not a tribunal filing, but a misstatement repeated in a pleading becomes a false statement to a tribunal (Rule 3.3; *fee_shifting_and_candor.md*). The same candor logic now drives the $3,100 credit: we found the error ourselves; Pinecrest should hear it from us first.

## 2. Facts (from the client file, as confirmed by the client on Oct. 26, 2026)

- **Contract.** Staffing Services Agreement eff. Jan. 15, 2024, one-year terms, auto-renewing; 60 days' notice to terminate. Governing law: State of Columbia. The 2026 hires fall within a renewal term; no termination notice appears in the file (**unknown — client has no further information**; §3's restriction applies during the term *or* for 12 months after termination, so the claim holds either way).
- **Payment.** §2: pay within 30 days of invoice; **1%/month interest** on late amounts; disputes must be given **within 15 days of receipt**, else invoice "deemed accepted."
- **Conversion.** §3: no direct hire of Juniper-introduced Personnel during term + 12 months "except upon payment of a conversion fee equal to 25% of the Personnel's first-year annualized compensation." **Juniper may waive the conversion fee in writing.**
- **§6 Limitation of liability.** No consequential damages either way; **unpaid fees and conversion fees are expressly *not limited***.
- **Exhibit C.** All disputes "arising out of or relating to" the Agreement, **including arbitrability**, go to **binding AAA arbitration, single arbitrator, Capital City, Columbia** (C.1). Prevailing party recovers fees and costs **"in any arbitration or in any action to compel arbitration"** (C.3). Survives termination (C.5).
